topic: causal representation learning; privacy inference; domain generalization; treatment-effect modeling
status: four cross-period audited full texts; bounded validation-design hypothesis with positive and negative evidence, not a causal meta-analysis or novelty claim
claim: In this sample, a method can use causal language or assumptions while its evidence comes from different levels: a theorem under a specified generative model; a synthetic attack with the true causal parent supplied; OOD benchmark scores for a style-deconfounding representation; or randomized online treatment-assignment outcomes. These are not interchangeable validations. The 2014 visual-cause paper explicitly scopes its experiments as simple theory/algorithm feasibility and observes about 40% initial manipulator failure before iterative causal-data training lowers it to about 6%; the 2022 privacy result is a constructed four-party synthetic case; the 2025 SDCL paper's benchmark improvements do not independently show that its latent style variable is the true cause; conversely, the 2024 ROI paper does report randomized online outcomes, with improvement in three of four conditions and an explicit exception. A testable methodological hypothesis is that requiring authors to state the level of causal validation and, where feasible, include an intervention/target-outcome test will better predict transfer than observational/OOD score gains alone.

counterevidence: The 2014 visual-cause paper does not rely only on observational accuracy: its workflow explicitly uses causal data/representatives and includes iterative manipulator evaluation, though on simple synthetic/MNIST tasks.
The 2024 rDRP paper demonstrates that randomized online outcome tests can be run in a causal/uplift deployment setting; results are positive in three settings, not all four.

OOD benchmark and synthetic attack results are still useful for specific generalization/threat claims; the proposal is to avoid treating them as proof of a different causal mechanism, not to dismiss them.
falsifiable_test: For methods claiming causal representations/mechanisms, preregister a validation ladder: (1) identify the estimand and structural assumptions; (2) evaluate observational prediction/OOD performance; (3) where ethically and operationally feasible, apply known or randomized interventions on the proposed cause and nuisance variables; (4) measure both intervention consistency and downstream task quality on held-out environments. Compare how well OOD-only versus interventional validation predicts transfer to a new site/domain or target outcome, across multiple method families. The hypothesis is weakened if observational/OOD results predict intervention-consistent transfer just as well, or if intervention tests do not improve reproducibility or decisions.
